

```{r}
library(phyloseq)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# 1. Read the combined MPA file explicitly specifying tabs and disabling quotes
kraken_data <- read_tsv("C:/Users/rkeen/Downloads/combined.txt", 
                         col_names = TRUE, 
                         show_col_types = FALSE)

colnames(kraken_data) <- c("Classification", "20241126", "20241203", '20241209', '20241216', '20241230', '20250106', '20250127', '20250203', '20250210', '20250217', '20250303', '20250310', '20250324', '20250331', '20250407', '20250414', '20250421', '20250428', '20250505', '20250512', '20250519', '20250526', '20250602', '20250609', '20250616', '20250623', '20250630', '20250707', '20250714', '20250721', '20250728', '20250804', '20250811', '20250818', '20250825', '20250901', '20250908', '20250915', '20250922', '20250929', '20251008', '20251013', '20251020', '20251027', '20251103', '20251118', '20251201', '20251209', '20251216', '20251222', '20251229', '20260105', '20260112', '20260120', '20260202', '20260209', '20260216', '20260223', '20260302', '20260309', '20260316', '20260323', '20260330', '20260406', '20260413', '20260420', '20260427', '20260504')

# 2. Filter down to Species level
species_only <- kraken_data %>%
  filter(str_detect(Classification, "d__")) %>%           
  filter(!str_detect(Classification, "t__"))              

# 3. Build the Taxonomy Matrix
tax_mat <- species_only %>%
  select(Classification) %>%
  separate(Classification, 
           into = c("Domain", "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"), 
           sep = "\\|", fill = "right") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Clean up taxonomic structural prefixes
tax_mat <- gsub("[kpcofgs]__", "", tax_mat)
taxon_ids <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:nrow(tax_mat))
rownames(tax_mat) <- taxon_ids
TAX <- tax_table(tax_mat)

# 4. Build the OTU (Count) Matrix (selects all columns with numeric read counts)
otu_mat <- species_only %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(otu_mat) <- taxon_ids
OTU <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# 5. Combine into Phyloseq Object
pseq_data <- phyloseq(OTU, TAX)
print(pseq_data)
```


```{r}
# 1. Transform raw counts to relative abundance (fractions/percentages)
pseq_rel <- transform_sample_counts(pseq_data, function(x) x / sum(x))

# 2. Convert the phyloseq object into a standard tidy dataframe for ggplot
plot_df <- psmelt(pseq_rel)

# 3. Lump all species outside the Top 15 into an "Other" category
# We weight the lumping by 'Abundance' so the 15 highest-percentage species stay split out
plot_df_cleaned <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(Domain = as.character(Domain)) %>%
  mutate(Domain = fct_lump_n(Domain, n = 5, w = Abundance, other_level = "Other"))

```


```{r}
my_colors = c('#264653','#4F6D54', '#005F73', '#0A9396', '#94D2BD','#C9E4C5','#FEFAE0', '#E9D8A6', '#E9C46A', "#CFA860", '#DDA15E', '#F4A261','#CA6702', '#E76F51', '#A83232','#FF4D6D', '#FF758C', '#FFB3A7' , "#4B3F72",  "#726E97", '#E0E4F0' )

my_colors2 = c( '#005F73', '#0A9396','#C9E4C5', "#E9D8A6", '#FEFAE0' )

# 4. Generate the Stacked Bar Plot
png("Domains.png", width = 1000, height = 400)
ggplot(plot_df_cleaned, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Domain)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors2, na.value = '#F5F5F5') + # <-- Applies the unique colors
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = "Relative Abundance", x = "Sample ID", title = "Taxoniomic Identification of Classified Reads") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
dev.off()
```
```{r}
# 1. Isolate species raw counts
species_raw_counts <- kraken_data %>%
  filter(str_detect(Classification, "s__")) %>%           
  filter(!str_detect(Classification, "t__"))

# 2. Extract and build the OTU matrix using numeric columns
otu_mat_raw <- species_raw_counts %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% as.matrix()
otu_mat_raw[is.na(otu_mat_raw)] <- 0

# 3. Build the Taxonomy matrix safely
# The "Additional pieces discarded" warning is normal—it just means sub-species tags were cleanly dropped
tax_mat <- species_raw_counts %>%
  select(Classification) %>%
  separate(Classification, into = c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"), 
           sep = "\\|", fill = "right", extra = "drop") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Clean up taxonomic structural prefixes (like s__ or g__)
tax_mat <- gsub("[kpcofgs]__", "", tax_mat)

# CRITICAL FIX: Use distinct, unique internal tags for row names to prevent the duplicate error
taxon_ids <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:nrow(tax_mat))
rownames(otu_mat_raw) <- taxon_ids
rownames(tax_mat) <- taxon_ids

# 4. Create Phyloseq object using absolute, unique row keys
pseq_raw <- phyloseq(otu_table(otu_mat_raw, taxa_are_rows = TRUE), tax_table(tax_mat))

# 5. Normalize counts relative ONLY to the classified species pool
pseq_classified_rel <- transform_sample_counts(pseq_raw, function(x) x / sum(x))

# 6. Melt into a tidy dataframe for ggplot
plot_df <- psmelt(pseq_classified_rel)

# ==========================================
# CRITICAL FIX STEP: REMOVE NA TAXA
# ==========================================
plot_df_cleaned <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(Species = as.character(Species)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Species)) %>%                    # <-- This drops the big grey NA bar completely
  filter(Species != "NA") %>%                    # Bypasses literal text string "NA" variants
  mutate(Species = fct_lump_n(Species, n = 20, w = Abundance, other_level = "Other"))
# ==========================================

# 9. Plot the relative abundance stack
ggplot(plot_df_cleaned, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    y = "Relative Abundance (% of Classified Reads)", 
    x = "Sample ID", 
    title = "Top 20 Species Profile (Classified Reads Only)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```


```{r}
png("my_plot.png", width = 1000, height = 400)
ggplot(plot_df_cleaned, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Species)) +
  # CRITICAL FIX: position = "fill" standardizes the Y-axis to 100% within each individual sample
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + # Formats the y-axis cleanly from 0% to 100%
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    y = "Relative Abundance (% of Classified Reads)", 
    x = "Sample ID", 
    title = "Top 15 Species Profile"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
dev.off()
```


bacteria only

```{r}
# 1. CRITICAL: Isolate Bacteria and rows that contain Genus level data
# We look for "k__Bacteria" (or "d__Bacteria") and ensure the row reaches a Genus "g__" tag
bacteria_genus_raw <- kraken_data %>%
  #filter(str_detect(Classification, "Bacteria")) %>%       # Keeps only Bacteria
  filter(str_detect(Classification, "d__"))               # Ensures it has a Genus classification

# 2. Extract and build the OTU counts matrix
otu_mat_raw <- bacteria_genus_raw %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% as.matrix()
otu_mat_raw[is.na(otu_mat_raw)] <- 0

# 3. Build the Taxonomy mapping table
# We only separate up to Genus since we are intentionally ignoring Species strings
tax_mat <- bacteria_genus_raw %>%
  select(Classification) %>%
  separate(Classification, 
           into = c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus"), 
           sep = "\\|", fill = "right", extra = "drop") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Clean up taxonomic structural prefixes (like g__ or f__)
tax_mat <- gsub("[kpcofg]__", "", tax_mat)

# Generate unique internal tracking tags for phyloseq
taxon_ids <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:nrow(tax_mat))
rownames(otu_mat_raw) <- taxon_ids
rownames(tax_mat) <- taxon_ids

# 4. Generate your phyloseq object
pseq_raw <- phyloseq(otu_table(otu_mat_raw, taxa_are_rows = TRUE), tax_table(tax_mat))

# 5. Extract to a long tidy dataframe
plot_df <- psmelt(pseq_raw)

# ==========================================
# FILTER & LUMP BY GENUS
# ==========================================
plot_df_cleaned <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(Genus = as.character(Genus)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Genus)) %>%                     # Drops missing Genus entries
  filter(Genus != "NA" & Genus != "") %>%       # Bypasses literal text string "NA" versions
  mutate(Genus = fct_lump_n(Genus, n = 20, w = Abundance, other_level = "Other"))
# ==========================================

# 6. Generate your 16-color high-contrast Polychrome palette

# 7. Render the Bacteria Genus plot (scaled to 100% of bacterial genus reads)
png("top20_bacterialgenus.png", width = 1000, height = 400)
ggplot(plot_df_cleaned, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    y = "Relative Abundance (% of Classified Bacteria)", 
    x = "Sample ID", 
    title = "Top 20 Bacterial Genera Profile"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
dev.off()
```
